name: Exemption by Descent (entry, work, and study without a permit)

qualifying_event.description: A non-Fiji-citizen who is a child, grandchild, or great-grandchild of a person who was a citizen of Fiji on 10 October 1970 (Fiji's Independence Day, a 'principal citizen') may be granted this exemption -- reinstating a category repealed in 2007. NOT a grant of citizenship: it is an exemption from needing any separate permit to enter, reside, study, and work in Fiji.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Documentation establishing the ancestral link to a person who held Fiji citizenship on 10 October 1970.

requirements.blocker_text: Child, grandchild, or great-grandchild of a person who was a Fiji citizen on 10 October 1970.
Must hold citizenship of another country and must NOT be eligible for registration in the Vola ni Kawa Bula (the iTaukei/Native Lands register).

evidence_required.document: Civil records establishing descent from the principal citizen
Proof of the ancestor's Fiji citizenship on 10 October 1970

outcome.duration_length: 3 years, multiple entry/exit, issued as a letter rather than a passport stamp

sources.title: Department of Immigration, Fiji -- Exemption by Descent: child/grandchild/great-grandchild of a person who was a Fiji citizen on 10 October 1970, must hold foreign citizenship and not be eligible for Vola ni Kawa Bula registration, 3-year multiple-entry exemption letter covering entry/residence/study/work without a separate permit

SAS Fiji (law firm) -- corroborates the amending instrument: Immigration (Amendment) Act 2023 and Immigration (Exemption by Descent) Order 2023, effective 10 October 2023, reinstating a category repealed in 2007

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Fiji). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- the hard requirements (eligibility criteria) are tier-1 Department of Immigration sourced; the tier-4 law-firm source is cited only to corroborate the amending Act/Order's exact citation and effective date, which the primary immigration.gov.fj page doesn't itself state -- not used for any hard requirement. STRUCTURAL FINDING, IMPORTANT NOT TO CONFLATE: this is an IMMIGRATION EXEMPTION (no permit needed to enter/live/work/study), NOT a citizenship grant -- it is capped at three generations (great-grandchildren) from a person who held citizenship at Independence in 1970. This is legally distinct from fj_citizenship_reacquisition.json (which lets FORMER Fiji citizens themselves reclaim citizenship as dual nationals, no generational cap found) and from fj_citizenship_by_descent.json (registration for children born abroad after 2009 to a currently-Fijian parent). An open question flagged by secondary sourcing -- whether time spent under this exemption counts toward the residency clock for naturalisation -- was NOT resolved in this research pass. No accompanying family members are covered by the exemption itself; each descendant must qualify individually. Reinstates a category that existed before 2007 and was repealed for 16 years, primarily relevant to the Indo-Fijian and other diaspora populations who left Fiji's indigenous-citizenship (Vola ni Kawa Bula) system after the 1987/2000/2006 political upheavals.
